## Archived Statements
### May 30, 2024
**General Aviation / Kailua-Kona, Hawaii**
A Robinson R22 helicopter made a hard landing near Ellison Onizuka Kona International at Keahole Airport in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii, around 8:45 a.m. local time on Thursday, May 30. The registration number is N333PJ. Two people were on board. The FAA will investigate.
Investigation and Other Information

## Archived Statements
### May 29, 2024
**Commercial Aviation /Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport**
An air traffic controller cancelled the takeoff clearance for American Airlines Flight 2134 because another aircraft was cleared to land on an intersecting runway at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. The event occurred around 10:30 am local time on Wednesday, May 29. The FAA will investigate.
Investigation and Other Information
**General Aviation / Myrtle Beach, South Carolina**
A single-engine Diamond DA40 landed on Highway 501 in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, around 12:55 p.m. local time on Wednesday, May 29, after the pilot reported engine issues. Two people were on board. The FAA will investigate.
Investigation and Other Information

## Archived Statements
### May 28, 2024
**General Aviation / Richvale, California**
A single-engine Schweizer G-164B crashed near Richvale,California, around 2 p.m. local time on Tuesday, May 28. Only the pilot was on board.The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will investigate. The NTSB will be in charge of the investigation and will provide any updates.
Investigation and Other Information
**Commercial Aviation / Raleigh, North Carolina**
jetBlue Airways Flight 369 landed safely at Raleigh-Durham International Airport around 11:20 p.m. local time on Tuesday, May 28, after the crew reported a possible hydraulic issue. Passengers deplaned on the runway and were bused to the terminal. The Airbus A321 departed from Boston Logan International Airport and was headed to Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport. The FAA will investigate. Contact the airline for additional information.  
Investigation and Other Information

## Archived Statements
### May 27, 2024
**General Aviation / Jackson, Mississippi**
A PZL-SWIDNIK PW-5 glider crashed into the Ross Bennett Reservoir in Jackson, Mississippi, around 1:50 p.m. local time on Monday, May 27. Only the pilot was on board. The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board will investigate. The NTSB will be in charge of the investigation and provide any updates.
Investigation and Other Information
**Commercial Aviation / Chicago, Illinois**
Normal operations resumed at 2:45 p.m. local time at Chicago O’Hare International Airport after United Airlines Flight 2091 aborted takeoff due to a reported engine fire around 2 p.m. local time on Monday, May 27. The Airbus A320 was towed to the gate where passengers safely deplaned. The FAA temporarily halted arrivals into ORD. The flight was headed to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. Contact the airline for passenger information.
Investigation and Other Information
**Commercial Aviation / Colorado Springs, Colorado**
Southwest Airlines Flight 1070 landed safely at Colorado Springs Airport around 8:20 p.m. local time on Monday, May 27, after the crew reported smoke in the cabin. Passengers deplaned on the taxiway and were bused to the terminal. The Boeing 737-700 departed from Denver International Airport and was headed to Tampa International Airport. The FAA will investigate. Contact the airline for additional information.
Investigation and Other Information

Seven individuals died in traffic crashes over the 2024 Memorial Day weekend. The counting period for the holiday was from 6 p.m. on Friday, May 24, through 11:59 p.m. on Monday, May 27, 2024.
The Missouri State Highway Patrol reported the following statistics for the holiday weekend:
**Traffic Statistics**
*   Crashes: 275  
*   Injuries: 161  
*   Fatalities: 7  
*   DWI arrests: 128
**Boating Statistics**
*   Crashes: 7  
*   Injuries: 7  
*   Fatalities: 0  
*   Drownings: 0  
*   BWI arrests: 6
**Comparison to 2023 Memorial Day Weekend**

# Memorial Day weekend sees seven traffic deaths in Missouri
During the 2023 Memorial Day holiday weekend, the Missouri State Highway Patrol investigated 287 traffic crashes, resulting in 117 injuries and 12 of the 13 fatalities. Additionally, there were 10 boating crashes, no fatalities, and two injuries. Troopers made 137 DWI arrests and eight BWI arrests. No drownings were reported.
**Details of Fatal Traffic Crashes**
Troopers investigated all seven of the traffic crash fatalities. Fatalities occurred in the following areas:
*   Troop C, Weldon Spring: 3 fatalities  
*   Troop A, Lee’s Summit: 1 fatality  
*   Troop B, Macon: 1 fatality  
*   Troop E, Poplar Bluff: 1 fatality  
*   Troop I, Rolla: 1 fatality
**Friday, May 24, 2024**
Rosa L. Rodriguez, 55, of Amarillo, Texas, died when another driver lost control of his vehicle, leading to a collision on Interstate 270 westbound in St. Louis County. Rodriguez was not wearing a seat belt and was ejected from her vehicle, which caught fire. A passenger in her vehicle and the other driver sustained serious injuries.
**Saturday, May 25, 2024**
No fatalities occurred.
**Sunday, May 26, 2024**
Crystal P. Hooper, 37, of Monroe City, MO, died after her vehicle overturned on U.S. Highway 61 in Marion County. Hooper was not wearing a seat belt and was ejected. A passenger sustained serious injuries.
Patrick L. Shelton, 37, of Benton, MO, died after being ejected from a golf cart and struck by another golf cart in Bollinger County. Neither driver of the golf carts was injured.
**Monday, May 27, 2024**
Dwayne C. Washington, 44, of St. Louis, MO, died after his vehicle struck a guardrail on Interstate 270 eastbound in St. Louis County.

# Memorial Day weekend sees seven traffic deaths in Missouri
Danny Luebbers, 18, of Salem, MO, died after a vehicle he was a passenger in experienced mechanical failure and struck a tree in Dent County. Luebbers was wearing a seat belt.
William F. Gorman, 89, of Independence, MO, died when his motortricycle was struck while crossing U.S. Highway 65 in Benton County. Gorman was wearing a helmet.
Ronald W. Moore III, 38, of Catawissa, MO, died after his motorcycle struck a guardrail on Interstate 55 in St. Louis County. He was wearing a helmet.
The statistics may change if late reports of deaths, crashes, or incidents occur, or if a fatality is determined to be caused by a medical condition.

# Memorial Day weekend sees seven traffic deaths in Missouri
During the 2023 Memorial Day holiday weekend, the Missouri State Highway Patrol investigated 287 traffic crashes, resulting in 117 injuries and 12 of the 13 fatalities. Additionally, there were 10 boating crashes, no fatalities, and two injuries. Troopers made 137 DWI arrests and eight BWI arrests. No drownings were reported.
**Details of Fatal Traffic Crashes**
Troopers investigated all seven of the traffic crash fatalities. Fatalities occurred in the following areas:
*   Troop C, Weldon Spring: 3 fatalities  
*   Troop A, Lee’s Summit: 1 fatality  
*   Troop B, Macon: 1 fatality  
*   Troop E, Poplar Bluff: 1 fatality  
*   Troop I, Rolla: 1 fatality
**Friday, May 24, 2024**
Rosa L. Rodriguez, 55, of Amarillo, Texas, died when another driver lost control of his vehicle, leading to a collision on Interstate 270 westbound in St. Louis County. Rodriguez was not wearing a seat belt and was ejected from her vehicle, which caught fire. A passenger in her vehicle and the other driver sustained serious injuries.
**Saturday, May 25, 2024**
No fatalities occurred.
**Sunday, May 26, 2024**
Crystal P. Hooper, 37, of Monroe City, MO, died after her vehicle overturned on U.S. Highway 61 in Marion County. Hooper was not wearing a seat belt and was ejected. A passenger sustained serious injuries.
Patrick L. Shelton, 37, of Benton, MO, died after being ejected from a golf cart and struck by another golf cart in Bollinger County. Neither driver of the golf carts was injured.
**Monday, May 27, 2024**
Dwayne C. Washington, 44, of St. Louis, MO, died after his vehicle struck a guardrail on Interstate 270 eastbound in St. Louis County.

# Memorial Day weekend sees seven traffic deaths in Missouri
Danny Luebbers, 18, of Salem, MO, died after a vehicle he was a passenger in experienced mechanical failure and struck a tree in Dent County. Luebbers was wearing a seat belt.
William F. Gorman, 89, of Independence, MO, died when his motortricycle was struck while crossing U.S. Highway 65 in Benton County. Gorman was wearing a helmet.
Ronald W. Moore III, 38, of Catawissa, MO, died after his motorcycle struck a guardrail on Interstate 55 in St. Louis County. He was wearing a helmet.

According to the Investigation, a 2006 Lexus GX 470 operated by Gedeon Mpay of Waterloo was traveling southbound on I380 when the vehicle suffered a tire blowout. This caused Mpay to lose control of the vehicle. The vehicle entered the west ditch and rollover multiple times before coming to rest on its wheels. The Buchanan County Sheriff’s Office was assisted at the scene by the Jesup Police Department, Brandon Fire Department, LaPorte City Fire Department and LaPorte City Ambulance. # Six skydivers, pilot survive plane crash near Butler Memorial Airport
The Federal Aviation Administration reported that the crash took place near the Butler Memorial Airport about 1 p.m.
By Greg Dailey
Published: May 25, 2024 at 9:46 PM UTC|Updated: May 27, 2024 at 2:15 PM UTC
Share
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google
BUTLER, Mo. (KCTV5) - Seven people survived a plane crash on Saturday afternoon in Bates County, officials stated.
The Federal Aviation Administration reported that a single-engine Cessna C206 crashed near the Butler Memorial Airport at about 1 p.m.
Preliminary information indicates the plane that crashed early Saturday afternoon was flying a skydiving mission, according to the National Transportation Safety Board.
The pilot and all six passengers were able to parachute from the plane before it crashed. The pilot was found at a hangar at the airport when members of the sheriff’s office arrived.
Everyone involved in the crash was treated and released at the scene. The FAA reported that seven people had been on board.
The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the incident.
A plane crashed near the Butler Memorial Airport on Saturday, May 25, 2024.(Bates County Sheriff's Office)
Rodney Rom took this picture of a plane crash at the Butler, Mo. airport. The seven people on board survived the crash.(Rodney Rom)

KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - Following a plane crash in Butler, Missouri, the Federal Aviation Administration investigated what caused the incident.
The FAA reported early Saturday afternoon around 1 p.m., that a single-engine Cessna C206 crashed near Butler Memorial Airport.

# The FAA says this is what caused a skydiver plane to crash near Butler Memorial Airport
##### **READ MORE**: 89-year-old Independence man dies in Benton County car crash
The aircraft had six skydivers jumping. One of the jumper’s parachutes deployed over the tail, which damaged the horizontal stabilizer and it went out of control, according to the FAA. The pilot jumped out of the plane and deployed a parachute. The aircraft crash-landed in a field in Butler, Missouri.
All seven survivors were treated and released at the scene.

May 26, 2024

Posted May 26, 2024 2:00 AM
Photo Bates County Sheriff
BATES COUNTY —A pilot and six passengers survived a small plane crash that occurred just after 1p.m. Saturday near the Butler Memorial Airport, approximately one hour south of Kansas City.
First responders found the single-engine Cessna C206 in a hay field east of the airport runways, according to the Bates County, Missouri Sheriff.
The pilot had been able to parachute from the plane prior to the crash and was located at a hanger at the airport. EMS treated everyone involved at the scene and released them, according to the sheriff's office.
The plane is a total loss. The Bates County Sheriff’s Office is assisting the NTSB and the FAA in their investigations. Authorities released no additional details including the name of the pilot.

BUTLER, Mo. (KCTV5) - Seven people survived a plane crash on Saturday afternoon in Bates County, officials stated.
The Federal Aviation Administration reported that a single-engine Cessna C206 crashed near the Butler Memorial Airport at about 1 p.m.
Preliminary information indicates the plane that crashed early Saturday afternoon was flying a skydiving mission, according to the National Transportation Safety Board.
The pilot and all six passengers were able to parachute from the plane before it crashed. The pilot was found at a hangar at the airport when members of the sheriff’s office arrived.
Everyone involved in the crash was treated and released at the scene. The FAA reported that seven people had been on board.
The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the incident.
A plane crashed near the Butler Memorial Airport on Saturday, May 25, 2024.(Bates County Sheriff's Office)
Rodney Rom took this picture of a plane crash at the Butler, Mo. airport. The seven people on board survived the crash.(Rodney Rom)

BATES COUNTY —A pilot and six passengers survived a small plane crash that occurred just after 1p.m. Saturday near the Butler Memorial Airport, approximately one hour south of Kansas City.
First responders found the single-engine Cessna C206 in a hay field east of the airport runways, according to the Bates County, Missouri Sheriff.
The pilot had been able to parachute from the plane prior to the crash and was located at a hanger at the airport. EMS treated everyone involved at the scene and released them, according to the sheriff's office.
The plane is a total loss. The Bates County Sheriff’s Office is assisting the NTSB and the FAA in their investigations. Authorities released no additional details including the name of the pilot.

The flight reaches a maximum altitude of 7,120 feet (2,170 m) and a top speed of 246 knots (456 km/h; 283 mph) during its 12-minute flight.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-auto1-40) The company aims to use the XB-1 to develop its Overturesupersonic airliner, of which the XB-1 is a roughly 1/3rd scale model.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-41)29 March In response to Venezuela's airspace closure to Argentina, the Argentine Government and United States Government lodges a complaint to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) to protest the closure, requesting that the airspace be reopened as a violation of the Chicago Convention.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-43)4 April US company Skydweller Aero completes the world's first unmanned flight of a large solar-powered aircraft.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-44)13 AprilIraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Kuwait and Israel all close their airspaces in response to the Iranian strikes in Israel.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-46)17 April The FAA implements a ground stop for Alaska Airlines and its subsidiary Horizon Air (meaning planes are not permitted to take off) after a notification by the airline. Alaska Airlines makes the request after an issue surfaced during a routine system upgrade essential for ensuring aircraft weight and balance, although the exact nature of the issue is not disclosed.

The airline states that it acted "out of an abundance of caution".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-47)18 April Kenya's highest ranking military officer, General Francis Ogolla, and nine other members of the Kenya Defence Forces are killed in the crash of a UH-1 Huey in western Kenya.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-49)23 April Two Royal Malaysian Navy helicopters collide over Lumut, Perak in Malaysia during a formation flight as part of a rehearsal for the upcoming Navy day parade. All 10 people on board the Leonardo AW139 and Eurocopter Fennec are killed.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-51)An Alaska Air Fuel Douglas C-54Dcrashed shortly after takeoff from Fairbanks International Airport. Both pilots, the only people on board, are killed.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-52)25 AprilSouthwest Airlines and American Airlines report large first-quarter economic losses, with Southwest losing US$231 million and American expecting to lay off over 2,000 employees during the remainder of the year. In addition, Southwest is to stop flying to Cozumel, Syracuse and Bellingham airports.

These declines have limited the airlines' abilities to order more aircraft in the near future, with Southwest cancelling some of its Boeing 737 orders for the year.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-53)30 April Australian low-cost airline Bonza which launched operations in January 2023, enters voluntary administration with all services suspended.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-auto-54)3 MayDick Rutan, older brother of Burt Rutan, dies at the age of 85 in [Coeur d'Alene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coeur_d'Alene,_Idaho "Coeur d'Alene, Idaho"), Idaho. The aircraft is diverted to Bangkok, Thailand.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_aviation#cite_note-59)27 May Following the closure of Porto Alegre Airport on 3 May for an undetermined time, due to flooding in the Rio Grande do Sul region, Brazilian airlines announces that limited services will be operated from Canoas Air Force Base. # **Preliminary Reports**
## **One Killed, Five Hurt in North Sea Training Accident**
### Sikorsky S-92A, Feb. 28, 2024,15 nm west of Bergen, Norway
A search-and-rescue (SAR) crew located five of the six crew members after the helicopter crashed into the sea near Sotra Island but had to return to base for fuel before locating the sixth. By the time a second flight found her, the 61-year-old nurse had been in the water more than 25 minutes. She was pronounced dead on arrival at the hospital; one survivor was hospitalized in critical condition and a second was described as seriously hurt.
The wreckage was subsequently recovered from a depth of 220 meters (720 feet). Records retrieved from the flight data recorder led investigators to conclude that the crash “cannot be described as a controlled emergency landing,” possibly explaining why the aircraft’s emergency floats did not activate. The accident, which prompted a brief safety standdown, occurred while the crew was training to conduct SAR operations.

Source: https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEB6zswFSJsLrL94NoYL6O74_oumald1Vr3VFfe4_ogwmFVzK_OUNV1rEzXcAe7grQ2P23ZgTKdtcsuIUMjpH0IX_wjsqLV4dCpnuIezV4psXYrxlG8ao89d6NIvMYTAi1DqCxUipMm0YdKlbBcVucds8yH4y3APh8NIFh1174SyKfUZZlqA3cC
Title: May 2024 Aviation Accident & Incident Summary
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
by Jim Timm
The following are the reports of aviation accidents and incidents that have occurred in Arizona from mid-April through May. We hope to use the following detailed accident information to develop safety programs, briefings, and posters/flyers that would help pilots learn from the mistakes being made by others and be able to take the necessary action to prevent them from having similar occurrences.
The number of accidents/Incidents have been very significantly up this past reporting period, and aviation safety has also not been the best because of a fatality that was incurred in one of the accidents. At least in all the other occurrences nobody got hurt. Things will have to improve as we go forward.
In continuing with the expanded scope of the report, we’re using information from the Aviation Safety Network (ASN), FAA, NTSB, and APA Members. This more inclusive information source suits our purpose of trying to get an idea of what is happening out there so we can help make flying safer.
In the meantime, here are the results from the above sources.
Date: **April 12, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
Location: Wilcox
Type: Piper PA-28-32-300
Injuries: 3 Uninjured
STRUCK OBSTRUCTION ON TAKEOFF
The Piper Cherokee 6 was departing Indie Motorsports Ranch when it encountered a 20-KNOT wind gust, which pushed them into a wall next to the runway and sheared off the left landing gear. The aircraft squawked an emergency on the Albuquerque Center frequency, and the center then provided flight following for the aircraft while it flew to Mesa Falcon Field where it made a safe landing. The full extent of the damage was unknown.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 13, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Scottsdale (SDL)
Type: Cirrus SR22
Injuries: 4 Uninjured
NOSE GEAR COLLAPSE
The nose Gear collapsed upon landing at Scottsdale. The damage that was incurred was minor.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 14, 2024**
Source: ASN
Location: Ak Chin (A39)
Type: Paramotor Powered Parachute
Injuries: 1 Fatality
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING

A “paramotor,” an Aircraft designation known as a Powered Parachute, sustained substantial damage subsequent to an impact with terrain during an apparent landing attempt northwest of Ak-Chin Regional Airport (A39).
No Pilot Certification Required.
Date: **April 14, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
Location: Payson (PAN)
Type: Team Rocket F1 (Experimental)
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING
The aircraft had departed from Glendale Airport, and upon landing at Payson the aircraft encountered a cross wind, and the aircraft bounced, and drifted to the right. The right wingtip contacted the ground, bending the right landing gear, and experienced a prop strike, damaging the engine mount. The NTSB assessed the damage to be substantial.
Commercial Pilot
Date: **April 17, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Phoenix Deer Valley (DVT)
Type: Cessna 182
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
STRUCK WHILE ON THE GROUND
While the Cessna 182 was holding short of the runway waiting to takeoff, and the rudder was clipped by another aircraft. The extent of the damage was unknown.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 17, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Phoenix Deer Valley (DVT)
Type: Pilatus PC-12
Injuries: 3 Uninjured
STRUCK ANOTHER AIRCRAFT ON THE GROUND
While the Pilatus was taxiing on a taxi way the pilot reported he had struck the rudder of a Cessna 182, The extent of the damage was unknown.
Commercial Pilot
Date: **April 17, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Casa Grande (CGZ)
Type: Cirrus SR 22
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
IN FLIGHT EMERGENCY
The Cirrus requested the nearest airport because of an engine vibration whenever power was applied. The controller suggested Casa Grande (CGZ) and verified that the pilot was declaring an emergency. The aircraft made a safe landing at Casa Grande airport.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 19, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB

Location: Pinal Airpark (MJZ)
Type: Piper PA-28-151 Warrior
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
INFLIGHT ENGINE FAILURE
The Piper Warrior had departed Coolidge, and while in cruise they encountered a catastrophic engine failure and made a Mayday call. They landed in a field 12 miles north of Pinal Airpark, and the aircraft damage was determined to be substantial.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **April 20, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Flagstaff (FLG)
Type: 1A-1125 Astra Jet
Injuries: 5 Uninjured
INFLIGHT ENGINE FAILURE
The Astra Jet had an engine failure, and an emergency was declared. The aircraft made a safe landing at Flagstaff, and the emergency was terminated by the Flagstaff airport AARF9 team.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **April 21, 2024**
Source: FAA
Location: Phoenix Goodyear (GYR)
Type: Cessna 210
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
GROUND FIRE
The aircraft caught fire while the pilot was running it up prior to flight. The pilot was able to exit the aircraft safely and requested assistance from the fire department. The pilot was checking the aircraft after its annual inspection, and the fire damage was substantial.
Commercial Pilot
Date: **April 22, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
Location: Benson (E95)
Type: Rans S-75 Courier
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER TAKEOFF
The Rans Courier lost fuel pressure shortly after takeoff and made an emergency landing in the desert. During the landing the landing gear collapsed and substantial damage was incurred.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 26, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Ryan Field (RYN)
Type: Piper PA-28R-200
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
GEAR UP LANDING
The Piper Arrow landed gear up at Tucson Ryan Field, and the NTSB assessed the damage to be minor.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **April 29, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident

Location: Glendale (GEU)
Type: Beechcraft BE-A36
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
GEAR UP LANDING
The Beech Bonanza landed gear up at Glendale Airport, and the damage was determined to be minor.
Private Pilot
Date: **May 1, 2024**
Source: NTSB, FAA Incident
Location: Near Marana
Type: Piper PA-28-180
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
ENGINE FAILURE
The pilot reported a rough running engine and landed in a canal on the final approach one mile short of the runway at Marana Regional Airport. Per the NTSB the aircraft was undamaged.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **May 1, 2024**
Source: ASN, NTSB
Location: Chandler (CHD)
Type: Piper PA-28-181 Archer
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING
The aircraft had departed from Falcon Field (FFZ), and while landing at Chandler Municipal Airport (CHD) the aircraft went off the runway, and struck a sign causing substantial damage to the aircraft.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **May 6, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Prescott (PRC)
Type: Cessna 172
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING
Upon landing at Prescott, the aircraft drifted off the runway into the sod between the runway and the parallel taxiway. The aircraft was ultimately towed to parking.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **May 9, 2024**
Source: FAA
Location: Lake Havasu (HII)
Type: Bushmaster-4P Amateur Built Amphibian
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
HARD LANDING
The aircraft lost power while turning downwind to land and made a hard landing. The aircraft ended up inverted on the ground. The extent of the damage was unknown.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **May 21, 2024**
Source: ASN
Location: Pleasant Valley Airport (P48) Closed
Type: Nanchang CJ-6A
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING

# **Preliminary Reports**
## **One Killed, Five Hurt in North Sea Training Accident**
### Sikorsky S-92A, Feb. 28, 2024,15 nm west of Bergen, Norway
A search-and-rescue (SAR) crew located five of the six crew members after the helicopter crashed into the sea near Sotra Island but had to return to base for fuel before locating the sixth. By the time a second flight found her, the 61-year-old nurse had been in the water more than 25 minutes. She was pronounced dead on arrival at the hospital; one survivor was hospitalized in critical condition and a second was described as seriously hurt.
The wreckage was subsequently recovered from a depth of 220 meters (720 feet). Records retrieved from the flight data recorder led investigators to conclude that the crash “cannot be described as a controlled emergency landing,” possibly explaining why the aircraft’s emergency floats did not activate. The accident, which prompted a brief safety standdown, occurred while the crew was training to conduct SAR operations.

by Jim Timm
The following are the reports of aviation accidents and incidents that have occurred in Arizona from mid-April through May. We hope to use the following detailed accident information to develop safety programs, briefings, and posters/flyers that would help pilots learn from the mistakes being made by others and be able to take the necessary action to prevent them from having similar occurrences.
The number of accidents/Incidents have been very significantly up this past reporting period, and aviation safety has also not been the best because of a fatality that was incurred in one of the accidents. At least in all the other occurrences nobody got hurt. Things will have to improve as we go forward.
In continuing with the expanded scope of the report, we’re using information from the Aviation Safety Network (ASN), FAA, NTSB, and APA Members. This more inclusive information source suits our purpose of trying to get an idea of what is happening out there so we can help make flying safer.
In the meantime, here are the results from the above sources.
Date: **April 12, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
Location: Wilcox
Type: Piper PA-28-32-300
Injuries: 3 Uninjured
STRUCK OBSTRUCTION ON TAKEOFF
The Piper Cherokee 6 was departing Indie Motorsports Ranch when it encountered a 20-KNOT wind gust, which pushed them into a wall next to the runway and sheared off the left landing gear. The aircraft squawked an emergency on the Albuquerque Center frequency, and the center then provided flight following for the aircraft while it flew to Mesa Falcon Field where it made a safe landing. The full extent of the damage was unknown.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 13, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Scottsdale (SDL)
Type: Cirrus SR22
Injuries: 4 Uninjured
NOSE GEAR COLLAPSE
The nose Gear collapsed upon landing at Scottsdale. The damage that was incurred was minor.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 14, 2024**
Source: ASN
Location: Ak Chin (A39)
Type: Paramotor Powered Parachute
Injuries: 1 Fatality
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING
texts.1:
A “paramotor,” an Aircraft designation known as a Powered Parachute, sustained substantial damage subsequent to an impact with terrain during an apparent landing attempt northwest of Ak-Chin Regional Airport (A39).
No Pilot Certification Required.
Date: **April 14, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
Location: Payson (PAN)
Type: Team Rocket F1 (Experimental)
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
LOSS OF CONTROL LANDING
The aircraft had departed from Glendale Airport, and upon landing at Payson the aircraft encountered a cross wind, and the aircraft bounced, and drifted to the right. The right wingtip contacted the ground, bending the right landing gear, and experienced a prop strike, damaging the engine mount. The NTSB assessed the damage to be substantial.
Commercial Pilot
Date: **April 17, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Phoenix Deer Valley (DVT)
Type: Cessna 182
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
STRUCK WHILE ON THE GROUND
While the Cessna 182 was holding short of the runway waiting to takeoff, and the rudder was clipped by another aircraft. The extent of the damage was unknown.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 17, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Phoenix Deer Valley (DVT)
Type: Pilatus PC-12
Injuries: 3 Uninjured
STRUCK ANOTHER AIRCRAFT ON THE GROUND
While the Pilatus was taxiing on a taxi way the pilot reported he had struck the rudder of a Cessna 182, The extent of the damage was unknown.
Commercial Pilot
Date: **April 17, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Casa Grande (CGZ)
Type: Cirrus SR 22
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
IN FLIGHT EMERGENCY
The Cirrus requested the nearest airport because of an engine vibration whenever power was applied. The controller suggested Casa Grande (CGZ) and verified that the pilot was declaring an emergency. The aircraft made a safe landing at Casa Grande airport.
Private Pilot
Date: **April 19, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
texts.2:
Location: Pinal Airpark (MJZ)
Type: Piper PA-28-151 Warrior
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
INFLIGHT ENGINE FAILURE
The Piper Warrior had departed Coolidge, and while in cruise they encountered a catastrophic engine failure and made a Mayday call. They landed in a field 12 miles north of Pinal Airpark, and the aircraft damage was determined to be substantial.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **April 20, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
Location: Flagstaff (FLG)
Type: 1A-1125 Astra Jet
Injuries: 5 Uninjured
INFLIGHT ENGINE FAILURE
The Astra Jet had an engine failure, and an emergency was declared. The aircraft made a safe landing at Flagstaff, and the emergency was terminated by the Flagstaff airport AARF9 team.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **April 21, 2024**
Source: FAA
Location: Phoenix Goodyear (GYR)
Type: Cessna 210
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
GROUND FIRE
The aircraft caught fire while the pilot was running it up prior to flight. The pilot was able to exit the aircraft safely and requested assistance from the fire department. The pilot was checking the aircraft after its annual inspection, and the fire damage was substantial.
Commercial Pilot
Date: **April 22, 2024**
Source: FAA, NTSB
Location: Benson (E95)
Type: Rans S-75 Courier
Injuries: 1 Uninjured
EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER TAKEOFF
The Rans Courier lost fuel pressure shortly after takeoff and made an emergency landing in the desert. During the landing the landing gear collapsed and substantial damage was incurred.
Private Pilot

Source: FAA Incident
Location: Ryan Field (RYN)
Type: Piper PA-28R-200
Injuries: 2 Uninjured
GEAR UP LANDING
The Piper Arrow landed gear up at Tucson Ryan Field, and the NTSB assessed the damage to be minor.
Unknown Pilot Certification
Date: **April 29, 2024**
Source: FAA Incident
texts.3:

Title: Aviation and Plane Crash Statistics | Updated 2026

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **March 2025:**
*   Lanhsa Flight 018, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32, crashed into the sea after overrunning the runway during takeoff from Roatán Airport. Thirteen of the 18 people on board lost their lives.  
*   A Trident Aviation DHC-5 cargo plane crashed in a field near Mogadishu, Somalia, following a technical failure, resulting in the deaths of all five people on board.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **April 2025:**
*   Tropic Air Flight 711, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan EX, was hijacked during a flight from Corozal to San Pedro. Due to low fuel, the pilot was forced to make an emergency landing in Belize City. Upon landing, the hijacker injured three of the 15 other people on board before being shot and killed by an armed passenger.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **May 2025:**
*   Air Panamá Flight 982, a Fokker 50 carrying 38 people, crashed after veering off Runway 27 during landing at Bocas Del Toro Airport (BOC/MPBO) on Colón Island, Panama. Of the 3 crew members and 35 passengers onboard, 12 were injured, but all survived the accident.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **June 2025:**
*   Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 en route from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick, crashed into a medical college building shortly after takeoff. The accident claimed the lives of 241 out of 242 passengers and crew, as well as 19 people on the ground. It was the first fatal crash and total loss of a Boeing 787 aircraft.  
*   A hot air balloon operated by Sobrevoar caught fire mid-flight and crashed near Praia Grande, Brazil. Eight of the 21 people on board lost their lives.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **July 2025:**
*   On July 24, Angara Airlines Flight 2311, an Antonov An-24 traveling from Ignatyevo Airport to Tynda Airport, crashed into a mountain during its approach to Tynda, Russia, killing all 42 passengers and six crew members on board.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **October 2025:**
*   Emirates SkyCargo Flight 9788, a Boeing 747-400BDSF, struck an airport maintenance vehicle and veered off the runway while landing at Hong Kong International Airport, resulting in the deaths of two people in the ground vehicle.  
*   Mombasa Air Safari Flight 203, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan on a domestic route from Ukunda to Kichwa, crashed near Kwale, Kenya, killing all 11 people aboard.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **November 2025:**
*   UPS Airlines Flight 2976, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F operating from Louisville, Kentucky to Honolulu, Hawaii, crashed shortly after takeoff, killing 14 people and injuring 15 others.  
*   An AirJet Angola Embraer ERJ-145 crashed at Kolwezi Airport in the DRC; all 29 people on board survived.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **January 2024:**
*   The 2024 Haneda Airport runway collision involved Japan Airlines Flight 516, an Airbus A350 from New Chitose Airport, colliding with a Japan Coast Guard De Havilland Canada Dash 8 aircraft during landing. While all 379 occupants of the Japan Airlines flight were evacuated safely, tragically, five of the six occupants aboard the Coast Guard aircraft lost their lives.  
*   Alaska Airlines Flight 1282, a Boeing 737 MAX 9 departing from Portland International Airport, experienced uncontrolled decompression when a plug covering an unused exit door blew out. Despite the harrowing incident, the aircraft made a safe return to Portland with all 177 passengers and crew surviving.  
*   A Jetways Airlines Fokker 50 crashed during a humanitarian aid flight from Mogadishu to Ceel Barde, Somalia. The aircraft ran off the runway upon arrival at its destination, striking a house and resulting in the loss of one of the four occupants.  
*   A Northwestern Air British Aerospace Jetstream crashed shortly after takeoff while transporting mine workers from Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, to the Diavik Diamond Mine in the Northwest Territories, Canada. Tragically, six of the seven passengers and crew lost their lives as the aircraft made impact with the ground 500 meters (1600 feet) from the end of the runway.
**February 2024:**
*   Air Serbia Flight 324, operated by Marathon Airlines using an Embraer 195, hit the landing lights during takeoff at Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport. The aircraft continued to fly for another hour before making an emergency landing back at the same airport, despite sustaining a large hole in its fuselage. Remarkably, all 111 occupants on board survived without injury.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **March 2024:**
*   In the 2024 Nairobi mid-air collision, Safarilink Aviation Flight 53, a De Havilland Canada Dash 8, collided with a Cessna 172. The collision resulted in the Cessna 172 crashing and killing both of its occupants, while the Dash 8 managed to land safely.  
*   LATAM Airlines Flight 800, a Boeing 787-9 traveling from Sydney to Auckland, experienced an in-flight upset that resulted in injuries to 50 passengers. Despite the incident, the flight landed safely at Auckland Airport.  
*   In the 2024 Malakal Airport collision, a Safe Air Company Boeing 727-200 on a cargo flight from Juba Airport undershot the runway and collided with an MD-82 while attempting to land at Malakal Airport, South Sudan. All seven crew members on board survived, with one sustaining injuries.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **May 2024:**
*   During Singapore Airlines Flight 321 from London-Heathrow to Singapore, carrying 229 people, the Boeing 777-300ER encountered severe turbulence, resulting in one passenger’s death and injuring 30 others. The plane made an emergency landing in Bangkok.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **July 2024:**
*   Gazpromavia Flight 9608, a Sukhoi Superjet 100, was on a ferry flight from Lukhovitsy to Moscow when it crashed during an emergency landing attempt near Moscow. Tragically, all three crew members lost their lives in the accident.  
*   A Saurya Airlines Bombardier CRJ-200ER crashed shortly after departing from Kathmandu Tribhuvan Airport on its way to Pokhara International Airport, resulting in the deaths of 18 of the 19 people on board.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **August 2024:**
*   Voepass Flight 2283, an ATR-72-500 flying from Cascavel Airport to Guarulhos International Airport in São Paulo, Brazil, entered a flat spin and crashed in Vinhedo, São Paulo, killing all 62 people on board.  
*   Thai Flying Service Flight 209, a Cessna 208 Grand Caravan traveling from Bangkok to Ko Mai Si, Thailand, crashed in a mangrove swamp shortly after takeoff from Suvarnabhumi Airport, killing all nine occupants.  
*   A Vityaz-Aero Mil Mi-8T helicopter crashed near the Vachkazhets volcano in Kamchatka Krai, Russia, during poor weather conditions, killing all 22 people on board.

opened.information:
Source: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/08/amazon-cargo-plane-crash-victims
Title: Pilots tried to abort landing seconds before deadly Amazon cargo plane crash
Chunks: 0,1,2
Officials in Florida on Tuesday said evidence collected from Saturday’s Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami international airport suggests the pilots considered aborting the flight’s landing before it crashed and killed five people on the ground.
At a press conference on Tuesday evening, officials from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) released data from the plane’s “black box” flight data recorder, which was recovered from the wreckage on Monday, indicating pilots initiated a “go-around”, or aborted landing, seconds before impact.
The NTSB said that ‌30 seconds before the end of the flight data recording, the nose ​landing gear and right main landing gear touched down, while 19 seconds before the end of the recording, the left main ⁠landing gear touched down.
A few seconds later, ​the ​brakes were released ​and the throttles were increased to values ​consistent ‌with go-around thrust.
The ​NTSB ​added there was no indication in the recorded data that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed.
Jennifer Homendy, the NTSB chair, said the pilots will be interviewed on Wednesday, and details from the cockpit voice recorder will be released publicly after that interview.
The NTSB will be conducting further analysis on the flight data and other available evidence to determine the cause of the accident, officials said.
Earlier Tuesday, officials identified the five people killed on Saturday – and said two more remained hospitalized in critical condition.
At a morning news conference, the Miami-Dade sheriff, Rosie Cordero-Stutz, also said both pilots of the Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767, which careered off the end of the airport’s runway and struck at least two vehicles, were released from the hospital after treatment.
The aircrew, whom she did not name, were the only two people onboard.
The sheriff identified Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Narajo, 53; Julio C Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47, as those killed on the ground.

All five dead and the two people most seriously hurt – men aged 79 and 32 – were in a Ford Econoline van that was hit by the aircraft, operated by the all-cargo airline 21 Air llc under contract to Amazon, while it landed after a flight from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and crashed through fencing on to a roadway.
The victims killed were employees of Professional Ocean Service Corporation, an aircraft contract cleaning company, which released a statement on Tuesday paying tribute to its dead workers.
“Our employees are far more than the people who work beside us each day, they are family, and they are deeply loved,” the statement said.
“Our hearts and prayers are with every employee and every family whose lives have been forever changed. We grieve with those who lost a loved one and pray for the healing and recovery of those who were injured.”
The lives of the families of the victims had been torn apart, Cordero-Stutz told reporters at the news conference.
“[We’re] trying to identify what happened and how it occurred, but for those families, they are going to be living with this for the rest of their lives,” she said.
“So it’s a very difficult time, and it’s very difficult on each and every one of these families.”
Investigators from the NTSB continued their examination of the crash site on Tuesday as the airport began to return to normal operations after three days of cancellations and delays.
At a press conference on Monday afternoon, Homendy said teams were working through a scene of “utter devastation” after the crash, which occurred after a thunderstorm.
The aircraft, she said, traveled about 1,300ft beyond the paved surface at the end of the runway and through a perimeter fence. The crash left a wide field of debris, including airbags and other parts of the destroyed vehicles, sections of the aircraft, and fencing.
“It’s pretty extensive,” she said. “Hard to see, and I’m sure it must have been very difficult for the responders as well. I would describe it in one word as devastating, utter devastation.”
Video showed the plane touched down far along the runway, prompting speculation its speed was too high to be able to stop safely.
Other factors being examined, Homendy said, were weather conditions before and during the landing, and the mechanical condition of the 32-year-old plane that was completing its third flight of the day.

Although the NTSB team would remain on site for about a week, she added, they would focus on recovering as much “perishable” evidence as possible, and not immediately determining a cause.
Some industry experts have said they believe the circumstances of the crash point towards pilot error. They include Robert Clifford, an aviation attorney who has handled cases in numerous commercial aircraft crashes spanning five decades.
“This appears to be a classic tailwind landing mistake where a pilot mistakenly or over-confidently decides to land with a tailwind instead of a headwind,” he said in a statement to the Guardian.
That, he said, “causes excessive touchdown speed and distance from the threshold, leaving inadequate stopping distance for the airplane’s braking and reverse thrust systems to handle”.
Clifford also noted the absence of any arresting devices or fencing at the end of the runway commonly found at other major airports. Homendy said on Monday the NTSB would be looking at that to determine its impact on the severity of the Miami tragedy.
Amazon, meanwhile, said it would work closely with federal investigators on the investigation. Homendy said her team would also examine the relationship between Amazon and 21 Air, the Miami-based aircraft operator.
*   _Reuters contributed reporting_

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
Emergency responders rushed to the scene but were unable to save the pilot. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have been notified and will investigate the circumstances surrounding the Oregon crash.
**Midair Collision of Vintage Aircraft Near Lancaster Kills Veteran Pilot Ryder Adams**| September 22, 2024
Amidair collisionbetween two vintage aircraft over Lancaster, California, on Sunday afternoon resulted in the death of Ryder Adams, 62. A respected member of the precision-flying Tiger Squadron, Adams was piloting a 1985 Nanchang CJ-6A when it collided with a Soviet-era Yakovlev Yak-52 around 12:50 p.m., according to local reports. The pilot of the Yak-52 survived with minor injuries after managing to crash-land nearby. The incident occurred in the skies above the Los Angeles suburb, with debris scattered near 47th Street East and 60th Street East. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation.

Officials in Florida on Tuesday said evidence collected from Saturday’s Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami international airport suggests the pilots considered aborting the flight’s landing before it crashed and killed five people on the ground.
At a press conference on Tuesday evening, officials from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) released data from the plane’s “black box” flight data recorder, which was recovered from the wreckage on Monday, indicating pilots initiated a “go-around”, or aborted landing, seconds before impact.
The NTSB said that ‌30 seconds before the end of the flight data recording, the nose ​landing gear and right main landing gear touched down, while 19 seconds before the end of the recording, the left main ⁠landing gear touched down.
A few seconds later, ​the ​brakes were released ​and the throttles were increased to values ​consistent ‌with go-around thrust.
The ​NTSB ​added there was no indication in the recorded data that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed.
Jennifer Homendy, the NTSB chair, said the pilots will be interviewed on Wednesday, and details from the cockpit voice recorder will be released publicly after that interview.
The NTSB will be conducting further analysis on the flight data and other available evidence to determine the cause of the accident, officials said.
Earlier Tuesday, officials identified the five people killed on Saturday – and said two more remained hospitalized in critical condition.
At a morning news conference, the Miami-Dade sheriff, Rosie Cordero-Stutz, also said both pilots of the Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767, which careered off the end of the airport’s runway and struck at least two vehicles, were released from the hospital after treatment.
The aircrew, whom she did not name, were the only two people onboard.
The sheriff identified Rolando Aleman Leon, 55; Yoel Rodriguez Narajo, 53; Julio C Pineda, 75; Carlos Acosta Fajardo, 53; and Javierkys Reyes Quevedo, 47, as those killed on the ground.
texts.1:
All five dead and the two people most seriously hurt – men aged 79 and 32 – were in a Ford Econoline van that was hit by the aircraft, operated by the all-cargo airline 21 Air llc under contract to Amazon, while it landed after a flight from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and crashed through fencing on to a roadway.
The victims killed were employees of Professional Ocean Service Corporation, an aircraft contract cleaning company, which released a statement on Tuesday paying tribute to its dead workers.
“Our employees are far more than the people who work beside us each day, they are family, and they are deeply loved,” the statement said.
“Our hearts and prayers are with every employee and every family whose lives have been forever changed. We grieve with those who lost a loved one and pray for the healing and recovery of those who were injured.”
The lives of the families of the victims had been torn apart, Cordero-Stutz told reporters at the news conference.
“[We’re] trying to identify what happened and how it occurred, but for those families, they are going to be living with this for the rest of their lives,” she said.
“So it’s a very difficult time, and it’s very difficult on each and every one of these families.”
Investigators from the NTSB continued their examination of the crash site on Tuesday as the airport began to return to normal operations after three days of cancellations and delays.
At a press conference on Monday afternoon, Homendy said teams were working through a scene of “utter devastation” after the crash, which occurred after a thunderstorm.
The aircraft, she said, traveled about 1,300ft beyond the paved surface at the end of the runway and through a perimeter fence. The crash left a wide field of debris, including airbags and other parts of the destroyed vehicles, sections of the aircraft, and fencing.
“It’s pretty extensive,” she said. “Hard to see, and I’m sure it must have been very difficult for the responders as well. I would describe it in one word as devastating, utter devastation.”
Video showed the plane touched down far along the runway, prompting speculation its speed was too high to be able to stop safely.
Other factors being examined, Homendy said, were weather conditions before and during the landing, and the mechanical condition of the 32-year-old plane that was completing its third flight of the day.
texts.2:
Although the NTSB team would remain on site for about a week, she added, they would focus on recovering as much “perishable” evidence as possible, and not immediately determining a cause.
Some industry experts have said they believe the circumstances of the crash point towards pilot error. They include Robert Clifford, an aviation attorney who has handled cases in numerous commercial aircraft crashes spanning five decades.
“This appears to be a classic tailwind landing mistake where a pilot mistakenly or over-confidently decides to land with a tailwind instead of a headwind,” he said in a statement to the Guardian.
That, he said, “causes excessive touchdown speed and distance from the threshold, leaving inadequate stopping distance for the airplane’s braking and reverse thrust systems to handle”.
Clifford also noted the absence of any arresting devices or fencing at the end of the runway commonly found at other major airports. Homendy said on Monday the NTSB would be looking at that to determine its impact on the severity of the Miami tragedy.
Amazon, meanwhile, said it would work closely with federal investigators on the investigation. Homendy said her team would also examine the relationship between Amazon and 21 Air, the Miami-based aircraft operator.
*   _Reuters contributed reporting_

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **March 2025:**
*   Lanhsa Flight 018, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32, crashed into the sea after overrunning the runway during takeoff from Roatán Airport. Thirteen of the 18 people on board lost their lives.  
*   A Trident Aviation DHC-5 cargo plane crashed in a field near Mogadishu, Somalia, following a technical failure, resulting in the deaths of all five people on board.
texts.16:
## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **April 2025:**
*   Tropic Air Flight 711, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan EX, was hijacked during a flight from Corozal to San Pedro. Due to low fuel, the pilot was forced to make an emergency landing in Belize City. Upon landing, the hijacker injured three of the 15 other people on board before being shot and killed by an armed passenger.
texts.17:
## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **May 2025:**
*   Air Panamá Flight 982, a Fokker 50 carrying 38 people, crashed after veering off Runway 27 during landing at Bocas Del Toro Airport (BOC/MPBO) on Colón Island, Panama. Of the 3 crew members and 35 passengers onboard, 12 were injured, but all survived the accident.
texts.18:
## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **June 2025:**
*   Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 en route from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick, crashed into a medical college building shortly after takeoff. The accident claimed the lives of 241 out of 242 passengers and crew, as well as 19 people on the ground. It was the first fatal crash and total loss of a Boeing 787 aircraft.  
*   A hot air balloon operated by Sobrevoar caught fire mid-flight and crashed near Praia Grande, Brazil. Eight of the 21 people on board lost their lives.
texts.19:
## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **July 2025:**
*   On July 24, Angara Airlines Flight 2311, an Antonov An-24 traveling from Ignatyevo Airport to Tynda Airport, crashed into a mountain during its approach to Tynda, Russia, killing all 42 passengers and six crew members on board.
texts.20:
## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **October 2025:**
*   Emirates SkyCargo Flight 9788, a Boeing 747-400BDSF, struck an airport maintenance vehicle and veered off the runway while landing at Hong Kong International Airport, resulting in the deaths of two people in the ground vehicle.  
*   Mombasa Air Safari Flight 203, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan on a domestic route from Ukunda to Kichwa, crashed near Kwale, Kenya, killing all 11 people aboard.
texts.21:
## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **November 2025:**
*   UPS Airlines Flight 2976, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F operating from Louisville, Kentucky to Honolulu, Hawaii, crashed shortly after takeoff, killing 14 people and injuring 15 others.  
*   An AirJet Angola Embraer ERJ-145 crashed at Kolwezi Airport in the DRC; all 29 people on board survived.
texts.22:
## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **January 2024:**
*   The 2024 Haneda Airport runway collision involved Japan Airlines Flight 516, an Airbus A350 from New Chitose Airport, colliding with a Japan Coast Guard De Havilland Canada Dash 8 aircraft during landing. While all 379 occupants of the Japan Airlines flight were evacuated safely, tragically, five of the six occupants aboard the Coast Guard aircraft lost their lives.  
*   Alaska Airlines Flight 1282, a Boeing 737 MAX 9 departing from Portland International Airport, experienced uncontrolled decompression when a plug covering an unused exit door blew out. Despite the harrowing incident, the aircraft made a safe return to Portland with all 177 passengers and crew surviving.  
*   A Jetways Airlines Fokker 50 crashed during a humanitarian aid flight from Mogadishu to Ceel Barde, Somalia. The aircraft ran off the runway upon arrival at its destination, striking a house and resulting in the loss of one of the four occupants.  
*   A Northwestern Air British Aerospace Jetstream crashed shortly after takeoff while transporting mine workers from Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, to the Diavik Diamond Mine in the Northwest Territories, Canada. Tragically, six of the seven passengers and crew lost their lives as the aircraft made impact with the ground 500 meters (1600 feet) from the end of the runway.
**February 2024:**
*   Air Serbia Flight 324, operated by Marathon Airlines using an Embraer 195, hit the landing lights during takeoff at Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport. The aircraft continued to fly for another hour before making an emergency landing back at the same airport, despite sustaining a large hole in its fuselage. Remarkably, all 111 occupants on board survived without injury.

### **March 2024:**
*   In the 2024 Nairobi mid-air collision, Safarilink Aviation Flight 53, a De Havilland Canada Dash 8, collided with a Cessna 172. The collision resulted in the Cessna 172 crashing and killing both of its occupants, while the Dash 8 managed to land safely.  
*   LATAM Airlines Flight 800, a Boeing 787-9 traveling from Sydney to Auckland, experienced an in-flight upset that resulted in injuries to 50 passengers. Despite the incident, the flight landed safely at Auckland Airport.  
*   In the 2024 Malakal Airport collision, a Safe Air Company Boeing 727-200 on a cargo flight from Juba Airport undershot the runway and collided with an MD-82 while attempting to land at Malakal Airport, South Sudan. All seven crew members on board survived, with one sustaining injuries.

texts.25:

*   Gazpromavia Flight 9608, a Sukhoi Superjet 100, was on a ferry flight from Lukhovitsy to Moscow when it crashed during an emergency landing attempt near Moscow. Tragically, all three crew members lost their lives in the accident.  
*   A Saurya Airlines Bombardier CRJ-200ER crashed shortly after departing from Kathmandu Tribhuvan Airport on its way to Pokhara International Airport, resulting in the deaths of 18 of the 19 people on board.

*   Thai Flying Service Flight 209, a Cessna 208 Grand Caravan traveling from Bangkok to Ko Mai Si, Thailand, crashed in a mangrove swamp shortly after takeoff from Suvarnabhumi Airport, killing all nine occupants.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **March 2025:**
*   Lanhsa Flight 018, a British Aerospace Jetstream 32, crashed into the sea after overrunning the runway during takeoff from Roatán Airport. Thirteen of the 18 people on board lost their lives.  
*   A Trident Aviation DHC-5 cargo plane crashed in a field near Mogadishu, Somalia, following a technical failure, resulting in the deaths of all five people on board.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **April 2025:**
*   Tropic Air Flight 711, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan EX, was hijacked during a flight from Corozal to San Pedro. Due to low fuel, the pilot was forced to make an emergency landing in Belize City. Upon landing, the hijacker injured three of the 15 other people on board before being shot and killed by an armed passenger.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **May 2025:**
*   Air Panamá Flight 982, a Fokker 50 carrying 38 people, crashed after veering off Runway 27 during landing at Bocas Del Toro Airport (BOC/MPBO) on Colón Island, Panama. Of the 3 crew members and 35 passengers onboard, 12 were injured, but all survived the accident.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **June 2025:**
*   Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 en route from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick, crashed into a medical college building shortly after takeoff. The accident claimed the lives of 241 out of 242 passengers and crew, as well as 19 people on the ground. It was the first fatal crash and total loss of a Boeing 787 aircraft.  
*   A hot air balloon operated by Sobrevoar caught fire mid-flight and crashed near Praia Grande, Brazil. Eight of the 21 people on board lost their lives.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **July 2025:**
*   On July 24, Angara Airlines Flight 2311, an Antonov An-24 traveling from Ignatyevo Airport to Tynda Airport, crashed into a mountain during its approach to Tynda, Russia, killing all 42 passengers and six crew members on board.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **October 2025:**
*   Emirates SkyCargo Flight 9788, a Boeing 747-400BDSF, struck an airport maintenance vehicle and veered off the runway while landing at Hong Kong International Airport, resulting in the deaths of two people in the ground vehicle.  
*   Mombasa Air Safari Flight 203, a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan on a domestic route from Ukunda to Kichwa, crashed near Kwale, Kenya, killing all 11 people aboard.

## 2025 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **November 2025:**
*   UPS Airlines Flight 2976, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11F operating from Louisville, Kentucky to Honolulu, Hawaii, crashed shortly after takeoff, killing 14 people and injuring 15 others.  
*   An AirJet Angola Embraer ERJ-145 crashed at Kolwezi Airport in the DRC; all 29 people on board survived.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **January 2024:**
*   The 2024 Haneda Airport runway collision involved Japan Airlines Flight 516, an Airbus A350 from New Chitose Airport, colliding with a Japan Coast Guard De Havilland Canada Dash 8 aircraft during landing. While all 379 occupants of the Japan Airlines flight were evacuated safely, tragically, five of the six occupants aboard the Coast Guard aircraft lost their lives.  
*   Alaska Airlines Flight 1282, a Boeing 737 MAX 9 departing from Portland International Airport, experienced uncontrolled decompression when a plug covering an unused exit door blew out. Despite the harrowing incident, the aircraft made a safe return to Portland with all 177 passengers and crew surviving.  
*   A Jetways Airlines Fokker 50 crashed during a humanitarian aid flight from Mogadishu to Ceel Barde, Somalia. The aircraft ran off the runway upon arrival at its destination, striking a house and resulting in the loss of one of the four occupants.  
*   A Northwestern Air British Aerospace Jetstream crashed shortly after takeoff while transporting mine workers from Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, to the Diavik Diamond Mine in the Northwest Territories, Canada. Tragically, six of the seven passengers and crew lost their lives as the aircraft made impact with the ground 500 meters (1600 feet) from the end of the runway.
**February 2024:**
*   Air Serbia Flight 324, operated by Marathon Airlines using an Embraer 195, hit the landing lights during takeoff at Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport. The aircraft continued to fly for another hour before making an emergency landing back at the same airport, despite sustaining a large hole in its fuselage. Remarkably, all 111 occupants on board survived without injury.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **March 2024:**
*   In the 2024 Nairobi mid-air collision, Safarilink Aviation Flight 53, a De Havilland Canada Dash 8, collided with a Cessna 172. The collision resulted in the Cessna 172 crashing and killing both of its occupants, while the Dash 8 managed to land safely.  
*   LATAM Airlines Flight 800, a Boeing 787-9 traveling from Sydney to Auckland, experienced an in-flight upset that resulted in injuries to 50 passengers. Despite the incident, the flight landed safely at Auckland Airport.  
*   In the 2024 Malakal Airport collision, a Safe Air Company Boeing 727-200 on a cargo flight from Juba Airport undershot the runway and collided with an MD-82 while attempting to land at Malakal Airport, South Sudan. All seven crew members on board survived, with one sustaining injuries.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **May 2024:**
*   During Singapore Airlines Flight 321 from London-Heathrow to Singapore, carrying 229 people, the Boeing 777-300ER encountered severe turbulence, resulting in one passenger’s death and injuring 30 others. The plane made an emergency landing in Bangkok.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **July 2024:**
*   Gazpromavia Flight 9608, a Sukhoi Superjet 100, was on a ferry flight from Lukhovitsy to Moscow when it crashed during an emergency landing attempt near Moscow. Tragically, all three crew members lost their lives in the accident.  
*   A Saurya Airlines Bombardier CRJ-200ER crashed shortly after departing from Kathmandu Tribhuvan Airport on its way to Pokhara International Airport, resulting in the deaths of 18 of the 19 people on board.

## 2024 Commercial Airplane Crashes:
### **August 2024:**
*   Voepass Flight 2283, an ATR-72-500 flying from Cascavel Airport to Guarulhos International Airport in São Paulo, Brazil, entered a flat spin and crashed in Vinhedo, São Paulo, killing all 62 people on board.  
*   Thai Flying Service Flight 209, a Cessna 208 Grand Caravan traveling from Bangkok to Ko Mai Si, Thailand, crashed in a mangrove swamp shortly after takeoff from Suvarnabhumi Airport, killing all nine occupants.  
*   A Vityaz-Aero Mil Mi-8T helicopter crashed near the Vachkazhets volcano in Kamchatka Krai, Russia, during poor weather conditions, killing all 22 people on board.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
Emergency responders rushed to the scene but were unable to save the pilot. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have been notified and will investigate the circumstances surrounding the Oregon crash.
**Midair Collision of Vintage Aircraft Near Lancaster Kills Veteran Pilot Ryder Adams**| September 22, 2024
Amidair collisionbetween two vintage aircraft over Lancaster, California, on Sunday afternoon resulted in the death of Ryder Adams, 62. A respected member of the precision-flying Tiger Squadron, Adams was piloting a 1985 Nanchang CJ-6A when it collided with a Soviet-era Yakovlev Yak-52 around 12:50 p.m., according to local reports. The pilot of the Yak-52 survived with minor injuries after managing to crash-land nearby. The incident occurred in the skies above the Los Angeles suburb, with debris scattered near 47th Street East and 60th Street East. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation.
**Small Plane Crash in Hawthorne, CA Leaves Two Critically Injured**| September 6, 2024
A single-engine Piper Comanche aircraft crash-landed on El Segundo Boulevard in Hawthorne, California, early Friday morning, critically injuring its two occupants. The plane, which caught fire upon impact, was believed to be preparing to land at nearby Hawthorne Airport when it crashed at approximately 12:40 a.m. Emergency responders quickly extinguished the flames and transported the pilot and passenger to a local hospital. Both were listed in critical condition.
A witness who was charging his Tesla nearby rushed to assist in extracting a man from the wreckage before a potential explosion. Remarkably, no injuries were reported on the ground, and surrounding buildings escaped damage. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have launched investigations to determine the cause of the crash.
**Wyoming Plane Crash Kills One, Injures Another in Ash-Scattering Flight**| September 1, 2024
A single-engine plane crash near Francs Peak in Wyoming's Absaroka Mountain Range resulted in one fatality and one serious injury on Sunday. Mary Lou Sanderson, 78, of Lake Havasu, Arizona, was killed in the incident, while the unidentified male pilot survived and was transported to a hospital in Billings with serious injuries.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
The crash occurred around 11:00 a.m. during a flight intended to scatter Sanderson's husband's ashes. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the crash of the American Champion 8GCBC aircraft, which also sparked a small fire in the remote area of Shoshone National Forest. A preliminary report on the Wyoming plane crash is expected in the next few weeks.
**Cessna Plane Crash in Oregon Suburb Kills Three**| August 31, 2024
A twin-engine Cessna 421C crashed into a Fairview, Oregon, townhouse on Saturday morning, killing three people. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) reported that the aircraft was attempting to land at Troutdale Airport when it encountered control issues, as indicated by air traffic control recordings. During its descent, the plane struck a power pole before crashing into a townhouse complex, igniting a fire. According to reports, two people on the plane were killed, along with a woman in the townhouse. NTSB officials stated that the incident occurred during a routine maintenance flight and that a full investigation could take up to 18 months.
**Engine Failure Cited as Potential Cause of Cessna Crash That Killed Pilot**| July 16, 2024
A pilot was killed when a twin-engine Cessna plane crashed into the Tred Avon River,in Talbot County, Maryland on Tuesday morning. Maryland State Police reported that the crash occurred at around 9:35 a.m. local time near Travelers Rest Circle in Easton. The pilot, who was the only person onboard, was found deceased in the water. The FAA said the pilot reported engine failure shortly before the fatal crash. Authorities say the University Research Foundation owned the plane.
**Crop Dusting Planes Collide in Idaho**| June 20, 2024
Two crop-dusting airplanes collided midair just west of the Arco airport in Idaho. One of the pilots was killed, and another sustained life-threatening injuries. The pilots have not been publicly identified.
The Butte County Sheriff’s Office received an emergency call at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time noting that the planes had crashed near the intersection of 3600 West and US 26/93.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) will investigate the crash. A preliminary report is expected in a few weeks.
**Man Killed in Auburn Plane Crash**| June 6, 2024
An unidentified man was killed on Thursday afternoon when the small plane he was piloting crashed into a building in Auburn, Washington. The fatal plane crash happened at around 12:15 p.m. local time near the 400 block of C Street Northwest. No one inside the building was harmed in the crash. Authorities are investigating the cause of the crash. A preliminary report is expected in the coming weeks.
**Plane Crash Kills Baton Rouge Plastic Surgeon Lucuis “Tre” Doucet and Two Children**| May 15, 2024
Three people were killed in a small plane crash in Williamson County on Wednesday afternoon. At 12:05 p.m., a local resident notified Williamson County 911 about a plane breaking apart mid-air and crashing. Authorities say the single-engine Beechcraft V35, was en route from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to Louisville, Kentucky, when it went down near Bending Chestnut Road in the Leipers Fork area, less than a mile from Natchez Trace Parkway.
The three deceased victims were identified as Lucius “Tre” Doucet, a plastic surgeon from Baton Rouge, and two of his adult children, Giselle and Jean Luc. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the fatal crash in Franklin.
The agency’s preliminary report included eyewitness accounts of a loud "pop” as the plane was overhead. Video footage showed pieces of the airplane descending through an overcast cloud layer. The debris was scattered in a fan-like pattern with a radius exceeding half a mile.
Officials recovered about 90% of the plane's wreckage, which included separated elevator rudders and wings, main fuselage fragments, seats, the instrument panel, engine, and propeller assembly. Some parts were found submerged in eight feet of water in a lake. According to the NTSB report, “[t]he deformation of the stabilizer spars on both sides exhibited features consistent with downward failure. A final report is expected to be completed in the next year.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
**One Dead in Modoc County, California Plane Crash**| April 9, 2024
A 69-year-old man was killed when a single-engine plane crashed between Alturas and Likely near County Road 60 in Modoc County. The plane was an agricultural plane used for crop dusting or spraying pesticides. However, it was not carrying any pesticides at the time of the crash. Authorities have identified the victim as Peter J. Spyres of Arbuckle, California. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the cause of the crash.
**Two Killed in Truckee, CA Plane Crash Identified as Liron and Naomi Petrushka**| March 30, 2024
Two Israeli tech investors were killed when a small plane crashed while attempting to land at Truckee Tahoe Airport. Liron and Naomi Petrushka were in a Daher TBM 700 plane that departed from Centennial Airport in south Denver at 4:22 p.m. MT with a scheduled arrival time at Truckee Tahoe Airport three hours and 16 minutes later. According to media reports, the single-engine turboprop crashed around 6:40 p.m. while approaching the airport.
Preliminary investigations by the Aviation Safety Network suggest that the plane missed its initial approach to the northeast-to-southwest runway at Truckee Tahoe Airport. The plane attempted a go-around maneuver, but instead went into a left-hand stalling spiral, ultimately hitting a tree near the Truckee River.
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has launched an investigation, which will focus on the actions of the pilot, the single-engine plane, maintenance records, and more.
**Ontario Family of Five Killed in Nashville Plane Crash**| March 4, 2024
A family of five from King Township, Ontario, Canada died on Monday night when their plane crashed on Interstate 40 while attempting to land at John C. Tune Airport in Nashville, Tennessee. Authorities identified the victims as Victor Dotsenko, 43, his wife, Rimma, 39, and the couple’s three children — David, 12, Adam, 10, and Emma, 7.

The plane, which caught fire upon impact, was believed to be preparing to land at nearby Hawthorne Airport when it crashed at approximately 12:40 a.m. Emergency responders quickly extinguished the flames and transported the pilot and passenger to a local hospital. Both were listed in critical condition.
A witness who was charging his Tesla nearby rushed to assist in extracting a man from the wreckage before a potential explosion. Remarkably, no injuries were reported on the ground, and surrounding buildings escaped damage. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have launched investigations to determine the cause of the crash.
**Wyoming Plane Crash Kills One, Injures Another in Ash-Scattering Flight**| September 1, 2024
A single-engine plane crash near Francs Peak in Wyoming's Absaroka Mountain Range resulted in one fatality and one serious injury on Sunday. Mary Lou Sanderson, 78, of Lake Havasu, Arizona, was killed in the incident, while the unidentified male pilot survived and was transported to a hospital in Billings with serious injuries.

A twin-engine Cessna 421C crashed into a Fairview, Oregon, townhouse on Saturday morning, killing three people. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) reported that the aircraft was attempting to land at Troutdale Airport when it encountered control issues, as indicated by air traffic control recordings. During its descent, the plane struck a power pole before crashing into a townhouse complex, igniting a fire. According to reports, two people on the plane were killed, along with a woman in the townhouse. NTSB officials stated that the incident occurred during a routine maintenance flight and that a full investigation could take up to 18 months.
**Engine Failure Cited as Potential Cause of Cessna Crash That Killed Pilot**| July 16, 2024
A pilot was killed when a twin-engine Cessna plane crashed into the Tred Avon River,in Talbot County, Maryland on Tuesday morning. Maryland State Police reported that the crash occurred at around 9:35 a.m. local time near Travelers Rest Circle in Easton. The pilot, who was the only person onboard, was found deceased in the water. The FAA said the pilot reported engine failure shortly before the fatal crash. Authorities say the University Research Foundation owned the plane.

Two crop-dusting airplanes collided midair just west of the Arco airport in Idaho. One of the pilots was killed, and another sustained life-threatening injuries. The pilots have not been publicly identified.
The Butte County Sheriff’s Office received an emergency call at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time noting that the planes had crashed near the intersection of 3600 West and US 26/93.

Three people were killed in a small plane crash in Williamson County on Wednesday afternoon. At 12:05 p.m., a local resident notified Williamson County 911 about a plane breaking apart mid-air and crashing. Authorities say the single-engine Beechcraft V35, was en route from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to Louisville, Kentucky, when it went down near Bending Chestnut Road in the Leipers Fork area, less than a mile from Natchez Trace Parkway.
The three deceased victims were identified as Lucius “Tre” Doucet, a plastic surgeon from Baton Rouge, and two of his adult children, Giselle and Jean Luc. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the fatal crash in Franklin.
